item.title: New Educational Programs for Agentic AI and AI Engineering
item.description:
New Educational Programs for Agentic AI and AI Engineering

Several new educational programs have been introduced to teach agentic AI, focusing on systems that can perform tasks, use tools, make decisions, and complete multi-step workflows with limited human intervention.

🔍 Overview

Agentic AI differs from basic chatbots through its ability to utilize tools and manage complex workflows. Key technical concepts include:

  • Agentic RAG: Combines retrieval capabilities with agent-based decision-making.
  • Multi-agent systems: Allows multiple specialized agents to work together.

⚙️ Key details

Comprehensive curricula for agentic AI are designed to go beyond basic prompt engineering, covering the following technical areas:

  • Architecture and Frameworks: AI agent architecture, LangGraph, and CrewAI for multi-agent workflows.
  • Development: LLM APIs, function calling, structured outputs, tool use, and API/system integrations.
  • Data and Memory: Vector databases, memory, and retrieval.
  • Operations: Agent evaluation, monitoring, observability, error handling, fallback strategies, and production deployment.

Practical workflows taught in these courses include automating repetitive tasks, connecting AI tools, creating business workflows, using AI for research and analysis, and designing practical AI use cases.

🚀 Availability

Program Focus and Key Features
IITM Pravartak Practical skills in AI agents, agentic workflows, AI engineering, RAG, and deployable agent systems.
IIT Roorkee (via Futurense) Combines generative AI fundamentals with agentic AI concepts.
PG Certificate in Building Professional Agentic AI with AIOps Combines agentic AI development with AIOps.
PG Certificate in AI-Driven LLM, SLM, Agentic RAG Development Focuses on language models (large and small) and retrieval-based AI systems.
Residential PG Diploma in AI/ML and Agentic AI Engineering Combines AI and machine learning foundations with agentic AI engineering.

#AgenticAI #AIEducation #LLM #AIOps #RAG

Source: Best Agentic AI Courses in India 2026 | Futurense

item.title: LogicMojo AI Certification Course Rated Deep Across Full Stack for 2026 Hiring
item.description:
LogicMojo AI Certification Course Rated Deep Across Full Stack for 2026 Hiring

LogicMojo published a ranking of AI certification courses for 2026, highlighting one programme that scores Deep on every layer of its six‑layer stack.

🔍 Overview

  • Hundreds of programmes now sit between ₹0 and ₹4L+ with near‑identical landing pages, hiring logos and “industry‑recognised certificate” claims.
  • A certification is described as a receipt, not a result.
  • The ranking is disclosed as published by LogicMojo, which is ranked #1.
  • Five expert reviewers (Suvom Shaw, Rishabh Gupta, Sankalp Jain, Monesh Venkul Vommi, Mohamed Shirhaan) fact‑checked the analysis.
  • Ten courses were scored on a single question: “If I start now with a job, a laptop and 8–12 hours a week, how quickly does this make me genuinely hireable?”

⚙️ Scoring Methodology

  • Six open pillars form the scoring framework.
  • Coverage is a weighted share of the 17 Table 2 skill areas (Deep 4 · Good 3 · Moderate 2 · Basic 1).
  • Reach is an indicative brand‑recognition index (author estimate, not enrolment data).
  • Seven tables and ten reviews support the scores.
  • Every section names where other options beat the evaluated programme.

📚 Curriculum Depth

  • Foundations start from Python and data handling; maths is taught as intuition tied to model behaviour.
  • Core ML covers ensembles, metric selection, imbalanced data and error analysis.
  • Deep learning includes real training runs, not just architecture diagrams.
  • The programme is the only one rated Deep on all six layers, including the three commonly skipped layers: production RAG, fine‑tuning and agents.

🚀 Delivery & Career Support

  • Live teaching delivered in Indian time zones.
  • Every project is peer‑reviewed and portfolio‑ready.
  • Support includes mentorship, resume preparation, mock interviews, job referrals and placement assistance.
  • The author could not verify any placement rate and therefore makes no claim about it.

💰 Value & Pricing

  • Depth comparable to programmes normally priced above ₹2L+ is offered at a mid‑band price.
  • No parallel catalogue of marketing, finance or product courses competes for curriculum attention; the syllabus is kept current.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a faster path to a job‑ready AI profile aligned with 2026 hiring needs.
  • Helps differentiate genuine depth from superficial certificates that merely act as receipts.
  • Enables learners to assess options side‑by‑side based on live teaching, curriculum quality, practical projects and career support.

#AICertification #JobReadyAI #AIEducation

Source: Top 10 Best AI Certification Courses to Become Job Ready Faster (2026)

item.title: OECD Study Finds Students Using AI Perform Worse Without Critical Assessment Training
item.description:
OECD Study Finds Students Using AI Perform Worse Without Critical Assessment Training

According to newly released data from the OECD’s Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), students who use artificial intelligence to help them study tend to perform worse at school than those who do not. The study, which collected data in 2025, represents the first time PISA has evaluated student performance since AI tools went truly mainstream.

📊 Scope of the study

The PISA study evaluated 15-year-old students across science, math, and reading. Key findings regarding student demographics and global trends include:

  • Global scale: The data draws from over 760,000 students across 91 countries.
  • Socioeconomic factors: After adjusting for socioeconomic status, students who never use AI generally outperformed those who do in science. AI use was found to be more common among students from relatively advantaged backgrounds, which likely reflects better access to hardware, stable internet access, and paid AI tools.
  • Geographic variation: AI utilization varies widely by country. For example, over 95 percent of Vietnamese students reported using AI tools, compared to just 60 percent in Japan.
  • Curiosity connection: The study noted that student curiosity levels correlate with AI use, peaking among daily users.

⚙️ Performance by AI task and frequency

The relationship between AI use and academic performance is complex, with results heavily dependent on how and how often the tools are used.

Method of AI Use Performance Impact
Summarizing texts or drafting writing assignments Relatively worse performance
Preliminary research or broad “help me learn” use Less of a performance drop
Weekly use to generally help learn Outperformed non-users (though not by much)
Weekly general help + critical assessment training All regular users outperformed non-users

Frequency of use also plays a significant role in student outcomes:

  • Daily or yearly use: Students who used AI daily, as well as those who only used it once or twice a year, tended to perform the worst.
  • Weekly or monthly use: Better academic results were seen among monthly or weekly AI users.

💡 Intentional learning vs. shortcutting

The study’s authors suggest that “moderate and intentional use of AI for schoolwork and learning” could have positive effects, especially when students are trained to critically assess the information they receive.

OECD director of learning and skills Andreas Schleicher explained the cognitive dynamics of using technology in education:

“In the same way that we do not become fit by watching sports but by doing sports, learning does not occur through the consumption of content, but as a productive cognitive struggle of the mind with new material,” Schleicher wrote. “Where technology enables or enhances that cognitive struggle, students will advance.”

Conversely, Schleicher added: “Where technology short-circuits the productive struggle of learning, it will undercut students’ development.”

#PISA #OECD #EdTech #AIinEducation

Source: Students who use AI generally score worse at school
